title: Bust Candidates
brief: Which players are likely to finish below their expected auction price in our 9-cat league, and why (role loss, crowded usage, shooting regression, age)? It must say that a bust label is about price, so each line should give a price at which the player becomes fine to buy.
summary: A bust in our league means a player whose auction price is above what he will give us in 9-cat. The most expensive risks are Maxey, Mitchell, Jalen Johnson, Haliburton, Barnes and Towns. The causes are crowded usage, managed minutes and age, and ESPN ranks or last season's prices push them up. Every player below has a price where he becomes fine to buy, so set a ceiling for each before 2026-10-18 and stop bidding when the room goes past it.

sections.heading: A bust label is about price

paragraphs.text: Calling a player a bust does not mean you should never draft him. It means the market values him wrongly at his current price. Fade him at a high price and take him when he gets cheaper. Liking or disliking the player plays no part in it.

A label only means something if you know its format. Many bust tags here compare a player to ESPN ranks or Yahoo ADP, not to 9-cat head-to-head value. ESPN ranks Bam Adebayo 15th, but the category experts put him in the 30s. ESPN ranks Mikal Bridges 26th, and the experts put him around 90th. Always check a price against the category experts and against what our league paid last season.

Play the prediction game. Project a realistic stat line and ask whether it really justifies the bid. Before the 2026-10-18 auction, write down a ceiling price for every name in this article. When bidding goes past it, stop and let someone else pay. Only 144 players get drafted, so anyone the experts rank past about 130 is worth 1 USD or a waiver claim.

When a team adds high-usage players, the existing star loses usage and assist upside, even if his minutes stay the same. Philadelphia is the clearest case. Maxey, Jaylen Brown and Edgecombe all share the ball with Embiid and LeBron. Every expert expects Maxey's usage to drop and prices him around picks 12 to 14, not top 10.

Portland has the same problem. Morant arrived, and Lillard and Scoot are back, so Avdija's 24.2 points and 6.7 assists will not hold, and Camara loses usage. Other shared-ball cases are Mitchell with Harden in Cleveland, Michael Porter Jr. with Randle, Siakam with Haliburton and Booker with Jalen Green.
Be wary of value that came from absent teammates. Bane's recent value came while Wagner, Banchero and Suggs were out. Trey Murphy faces the same drop now that Dejounte Murray is back.
In weeks 1 to 3, track shot attempts and assists in games where every star plays. If the usage loss shows up, sell before the 2027-03-04 trade deadline while his name still carries value.

When many players on one team have career years at once, expect some of them to regress, often together. Dosunmu's 3P% jumped from 33 to 44, his FT% from 78 to 88, and his steal rate is high. Pay him no more than a few dollars. Barnes's FG% rose to 50.7 while his threes fell. Holmgren's 65% two-point shooting and Jerome's 15-game sample also need to prove they can repeat. Ace Bailey's late-season numbers were inflated.

FG% and FT% are team ratios, so shooting problems hurt most on high volume. Edgecombe shoots a projected 43.8% on 13 shots a game, and Peterson 45.2% on about 14.5. Price them as late bench pieces, not as category anchors.

sections.heading: Age: no path above the projection

paragraphs.text: A player who has been in the league a long time is probably who he is. Projections are a median outcome. Veterans like Tobias Harris have no realistic path above theirs, so when two players project the same, take the younger one with the wider range.

Age turns into a bust risk when the price is high. Harden is 37, Davis 33, Siakam 32, and Towns and Mitchell are 30. Kawhi's knee leads to load management. For these players the main risk is games played. Rest matters most in our playoff weeks 19 to 21. Toronto and Philadelphia each have three back-to-backs in those weeks.
Age alone does not make a bust. Giannis, Kyrie Irving, Lillard, McCollum and Gobert carry age flags but are fair or cheap at their prices. Curry and LeBron are fine once you cap the bid.

The sources split on Durant. One side points to his age of 37. ESPN values him at only 26 USD, and media day reports suggest fewer than 36 minutes, with a drop to 33 hurting him. The other side is the category experts, who still see first-round value. Our view is that the mid 40s USD is fine if he keeps about 36 minutes. The projections also split on Morant: Yahoo has 5.7 assists on 13 shots, ESPN 7.2 on 16. That gap is why he is only a cheap flyer.
Let ESPN-anchored managers overpay for Davis, Bam, White, Kawhi, Siakam and Mikal Bridges. Spend the saved money where the market sits below the experts, such as Kyrie Irving near 10 USD.

Once the season starts, check minutes, shot attempts and FG% for every player you bought at a bust-risk price. Waivers run daily on FAB, with a maximum of 6 adds per week. Handcuffs like Nembhard, Drummond and Huff are waiver adds when the starter ahead of them gets hurt, not auction buys.
